components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled, solid action per view.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--phosphor-signal, #2dd4bf); color: var(--scope-black, #0a0f0d); font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.92rem; padding: 13px 30px; border: 1px solid transparent; clip-path: polygon(10px 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%, 0 10px); cursor: pointer; transition: filter 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.15); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--phosphor-signal, #2dd4bf); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: transparent; color: var(--text, #e5ede8); font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.92rem; padding: 13px 30px; border: 1px solid var(--graticule-line, #1f3a2c); clip-path: polygon(10px 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%, 0 10px); cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.2s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: var(--phosphor-signal, #2dd4bf); color: var(--phosphor-signal, #2dd4bf); }

components.name: Contact Card
components.description: The system's signature card: idle steel corner brackets that light up phosphor-green when hovered or active, like a radar contact locking on.
components.html:
J'ai des bases

Je veux choisir mes composants avec de l'aide.
components.css: .ds-chip-card { position: relative; background: var(--panel, #0f1a15); border: 1px solid var(--graticule-line, #1f3a2c); padding: 26px; } .ds-chip-card::before, .ds-chip-card::after { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 12px; height: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--graticule-line, #1f3a2c); opacity: 0.7; transition: border-color 0.2s, opacity 0.2s; } .ds-chip-card::before { top: -1px; left: -1px; border-right: none; border-bottom: none; } .ds-chip-card::after { bottom: -1px; right: -1px; border-left: none; border-top: none; } .ds-chip-card:hover::before, .ds-chip-card:hover::after { border-color: var(--phosphor-signal, #2dd4bf); opacity: 1; }

components.name: Radar Blip Tag
components.description: A single detected-contact marker used in the hero radar scope: a dot plus a monospace data tag, with a distinct 'detected' (locked-on) state.
components.html: CARTE MÈRE · OK
components.css: .ds-radar-blip { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; } .ds-radar-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--phosphor-signal-dim, #1a9c8a); box-shadow: 0 0 6px 1px rgba(45,212,191,0.5); } .ds-radar-tag { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.66rem; letter-spacing: 0.4px; color: var(--text-dim, #7d9186); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-detected .ds-radar-dot { background: var(--phosphor-signal, #2dd4bf); animation: ds-radar-pulse 2.4s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-detected .ds-radar-tag { color: var(--phosphor-signal, #2dd4bf); } @keyframes ds-radar-pulse { 0%, 100% { box-shadow: 0 0 6px 1px rgba(45,212,191,0.5); } 50% { box-shadow: 0 0 14px 4px rgba(45,212,191,0.75); } }

narrative.overview: PC Radar reads as an air-traffic-control scope, not a gadget showroom or a minimal SaaS dashboard. Every component a visitor adds is treated as a contact: it appears on the scope, gets a bearing and a data tag, and either locks on (compatible, phosphor-green) or drops off (incompatible). The metaphor is chosen deliberately because it does real work for the product — scanning for compatibility is the site's actual mechanism, not a decorative wrapper around it. The system stays dark and instrument-like at all times: a scope room is dim by design so the glowing signal reads clearly. Density is calm, not cluttered.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground with exactly two accent registers: phosphor green (signal/primary/detection) and instrument amber (value/selection/warning)
Monospace type reserved for data and status labels, never used as a generic tech costume on body copy
Corner bracket reticles replace rounded corners and drop shadows as the primary shape language
Glow is a signal effect reserved for active/detected phosphor-green elements, never decorative

rules.name: The Two-Accent Rule
rules.body: Only phosphor green and instrument amber ever carry meaning. A new feature needing an accent reuses one of these two by role rather than introducing a third.

rules.name: The Signal Glow Rule
rules.body: Glow is reserved for phosphor-green signal elements in an active state. It never decorates a neutral or amber element.

rules.name: The Data-Only Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace type appears only on data, status, or measurement content, never as a stylistic label on ordinary UI copy.

rules.name: The Flat-Scope Rule
rules.body: Cards never lift on hover via shadow; a locked/selected state is shown by bracket color, not elevation.

dos: Do keep monospace exclusively for data/status content.
Do use the corner-bracket reticle as the one recurring shape signature across cards.
Do reserve glow for phosphor-green signal states only.
donts: Don't add a kicker/eyebrow label above a section heading.
Don't add decorative sequence numbers to a set of cards that isn't a true ordered process.
Don't introduce a third accent color outside phosphor green and instrument amber.
